Assert that conditions hold

Source: R/assert.R
assert.Rd

Verify that every row satisfies all specified conditions, like Stata's assert. Stop with an error if any condition fails; otherwise, return the original data invisibly.

Usage

assert(.data, ..., .by = NULL)

Arguments

.data

A data frame, tibble, or data.table.

...

<data-masking> One or more logical conditions using columns of .data. Each must return one value per row, or one value recycled across the current group. Every condition must be TRUE for every row.

.by

<tidy-select> Optional grouping variables. Summaries such as mean(x) are evaluated within each group. Existing groups are used when omitted. To supply .by for grouped data, first call dplyr::ungroup(), as required by dplyr::mutate().

Value

.data, unchanged and invisibly, including its classes, grouping, and attributes, if all conditions pass. Failed conditions raise an error.

Details

Both FALSE and NA count as failures. Errors report the number of failing rows for each condition, including missing results, and the first five failing row numbers. A failed group-level condition counts every row in that group.

Unlike Stata, x > 0 fails when x is missing. Use is.na(x) | x > 0 to allow missing values.

See also

Other data checking functions: is_first(), keys, stata_merge()

Examples

scores <- data.frame(
  class = c("A", "A", "B", "B"),
  score = c(80, 90, 55, NA_real_)
)
scores
#>   class score
#> 1     A    80
#> 2     A    90
#> 3     B    55
#> 4     B    NA

# Pass: every nonmissing score is at least 50
assert(scores, is.na(score) | score >= 50)

# Fail: row 3 is below 60, and row 4 is missing
try(assert(scores, score >= 60))
#> Error in assert(scores, score >= 60) : Assertion failed:
#> • `score >= 60`: 2 contradictions (1 missing) in 4 rows; rows 3, 4
